title: Fleet Lifeline dashboard and autoscale controls — prototype & review
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: Deliver a lightweight, scannable console surface for dedicated GPU fleets that surfaces fleet vitality (latency, error trends, memory pressure), exposes safe autoscale controls, and provides friction-free burst windows for short-term demand. Scope: 1) Fleet Lifeline overview card for at-a-glance status; 2) Autoscale quick-actions (scale up/down, pin capacity, schedule window); 3) Burst presets and temporary capacity slider with clear cost impact; 4) Deep-dive flyout for series charts and recent incidents; 5) Small-device layout for SRE mobile review. Outcome: a vetted Figma prototype, annotated handoff tokens, and a short usability report with 5 recommended tweaks.
design_decisions: Single-row Lifeline: condensed row per GPU pool showing vitality waveform, SLO badge, and cost delta — trades detailed charts for rapid scanning
Three-tier signal color system (green/amber/crimson) with explicit age-based decay to avoid stale green states
Autoscale Quick Actions: primary CTA is 'Request Capacity' which triggers safe defaults (max 2x burst) to protect shared infra
Burst presets are time-boxed with immediate preview of cost estimate (30m/2h/24h) and automatic reversion
Accessible controls: keyboard-first focus order, labelled sliders, and ARIA alerts for action confirmations
tradeoffs: Condensed row reduces initial cognitive load but requires a flyout for detailed diagnostics — increases click-to-full-context
Conservative default burst caps lower risk of runaway spend but may frustrate high-throughput customers; exposed override requires approver flow (future work)
Showing cost estimates inline increases surface complexity; we prioritize short, relative deltas vs. raw dollar numbers to reduce noise
acceptance_criteria: Prototype (Figma) includes overview row, flyout detail, autoscale quick actions, and burst preset modal
Handoff tokens and component specs exported to tokens library and a11y checklist attached
Usability test with 6 engineers/SREs completed, at least 4/6 can complete 'create burst window' in under 90s without help
Design reviewed and signed off by PM and Eng lead; implementation tasks scoped and linked to ENG backlog
